summary: Joseph Kaynen Gurley was sentenced Tuesday to life without parole for the 2024 murder at a Daphne apartment complex, the District Attorney's office and local stations reported. Foley police are investigating the shooting of a 16-year-old in a car, which they believe was accidental, and the jail booked 16 people on criminal charges dated Tuesday, including a Robertsdale child-abuse arrest.

entries.title: Life without parole: Joseph Kaynen Gurley
body: Joseph Kaynen Gurley, 26, was sentenced Tuesday, Nov. 10, to life in prison without the possibility of parole on his murder and attempted murder convictions, WKRG reported; the Baldwin County District Attorney's office updated its Aug. 20 post to say he received life without parole. FOX10 reported two life sentences.

A Baldwin County jury convicted Gurley in August after a four-day trial in a shooting on March 31, 2024, at an apartment complex off County Road 64 in Daphne that killed one man and wounded another, according to the District Attorney's office. Prosecutor Patrick Doggett tried the case; Daphne police investigated.

entries.title: Terrorist-threat arrest near Foley schools: Gregory McGowen
body: Foley police said officers were called at about 7:40 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, to a report of a man with a gun near 9th Avenue and South Oak Street, close to two Foley schools, which secured their buildings. Police said Gregory McGowen, 59, of Foley, had no weapon on him when officers made contact; a replica firearm, which police said was a BB gun, was recovered a short distance away, WKRG reported.

Police said he was first charged with menacing, which they described as a Class B misdemeanor, and that the charge was upgraded to making a terrorist threat in the first degree, which police described as a Class B felony, because of the disruption at the schools. Alabama law allows 2 to 20 years for a Class B felony. The jail roster lists him booked by Foley police Nov. 10 on the terrorist-threat charge and an aggravated assault/menacing charge with a weapon; he was in custody when the roster was read early Wednesday.

entries.title: Teen shot in vehicle: Foley police investigating
body: Foley police said they received a report at about 2:45 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, of a 16-year-old with a gunshot wound. Police said three juveniles were riding in a car near North Pine Street when a gun went off and struck the teen in the torso, WKRG reported. The teen was treated at a hospital and was in stable condition.

Investigators said they believe the shooting was accidental, have identified and interviewed everyone involved, and do not believe there is a threat to the public. Police said criminal charges are possible. No one has been named.

entries.title: Child abuse arrest: Kameron J. Jackson
body: Kameron J. Jackson, 19, was booked into the Baldwin County jail Tuesday, Nov. 10, on an arrest by Robertsdale police dated Nov. 9, according to the jail roster. No police statement or news report was found.

The roster lists one booked charge, torture or willful abuse of a child, in the family category — a charge of deliberately abusing or cruelly mistreating a child. He was in custody when the roster was read early Wednesday.

entries.title: Obscene material arrest: Michael Ryan Cain
body: Michael Ryan Cain, 22, was arrested by the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office at 12:06 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, according to the jail roster. No sheriff's office statement or news report was found.
The roster lists two booked counts of distributing obscene material — a charge of distributing material the law defines as obscene. He was in custody when the roster was read early Wednesday.

entries.title: Other arrests Nov. 9–10: Christal Irene Pryear, Bradley Terrell Heard, Shawn Derek Wilson, Erick Stromas
body: Christal Irene Pryear, 31, was arrested by Orange Beach police at 9:42 p.m. Monday, Nov. 9, and booked on charges of attempting to elude a police officer and second-degree marijuana possession; she was in custody. Bradley Terrell Heard, 33, was arrested by Gulf Shores police Nov. 9 and booked on a charge of receiving a stolen vehicle; the roster shows him released Nov. 10.

Shawn Derek Wilson, 39, was arrested by the sheriff's office at 9:22 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10, and booked on charges of harassment of a family member and obstructing governmental operations. Erick Stromas, 19, was arrested by Gulf Shores police Nov. 10 and booked as a fugitive from justice — held on a warrant from another state or jurisdiction. Both were in custody. All information is from the jail roster.

entries.title: Drug trafficking case, bond set: Arvia Lloyd Allen
body: District Judge Grant Blackburn set bond at $114,500 on all charges against Arvia Lloyd Allen, 36, at a court appearance Monday, Nov. 9, WKRG reported. Allen was arrested Friday, Nov. 6, at a home in Foley, where investigators spent several hours and removed evidence, according to the station.

WKRG reported the charges include drug trafficking involving cocaine, methamphetamine, marijuana and Xanax. The jail roster lists six booked charges, including drug trafficking and being a drunk or drug addict in possession of a firearm. The roster shows him released Nov. 10.

entries.title: Daphne solicitation operation: former Fairhope officer among 12 charged
body: One of the 12 men charged in a Daphne police operation on Friday, Nov. 6, is Jonathan Fender, a former Fairhope police officer, Daphne police said, according to FOX10. The Fairhope Police Department told the station Fender left the department in February for a private-sector job.

Police said the multi-agency operation targeted people trying to buy sex along the Interstate 10 corridor. All 12 men face solicitation charges, and three face other charges, including attempting to elude, resisting arrest and marijuana possession, FOX10 reported. Investigators said no actual victims were involved in the sting.

entries.title: Elder exploitation arrest: Charlene Sue Moorere
body: Sheriff's deputies booked Charlene Sue Moorere, 57, into the county jail on Monday, Nov. 9, according to the jail roster, which gives an arrest stamp of 5:20 p.m. Nov. 2. She was in custody when the roster was read early Tuesday.

She was booked on a charge of first-degree financial exploitation of an elderly person — taking or misusing an older person's money or property. Deputies booked two other people on the same charge Nov. 8; the roster does not say whether the cases are connected.

entries.title: Attempting-to-elude arrests: Aaron Steven Wright, Jaden Tymerius Williams
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Aaron Steven Wright, 54, at 9:55 a.m. Monday, Nov. 9, according to the jail roster. Bay Minette police arrested Jaden Tymerius Williams, 21, who was booked Nov. 9 with an arrest stamp of 3:56 a.m. Nov. 10. Both were in custody when the roster was read.

Each was booked on a charge of attempting to elude a law enforcement officer — fleeing from police after a signal to stop. Wright was also booked on three counts of violating a release order, and Williams on a release-order violation and a failure-to-appear charge. The roster does not connect the two arrests.

entries.title: Beach-town drug arrests: Stanley Kyle Wilson, Natravious Tavon Saffold, Lamycal Decree Mitchell
body: Orange Beach police arrested Stanley Kyle Wilson, 42, early Monday, Nov. 9, on charges of drunk driving, improper lane usage, possession of dangerous drugs and drug paraphernalia, according to the jail roster.

Gulf Shores police booked Natravious Tavon Saffold, 23, on marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia charges, and Lamycal Decree Mitchell, 20, on second-degree marijuana possession, drug paraphernalia and possession of a synthetic narcotic — a lab-made drug such as synthetic cannabinoids. All three were booked Nov. 9 and released the same day, the roster shows.
